settings_audit_no_events_hint: Issue changes, member and role changes, and security events will show up here.
settings_audit_no_matching_hint: Try a wider date range or clear the filters.
settings_dev_bitbucket_desc: Link a Bitbucket Cloud repository so pull requests and commits update issues, with build and approval status on each issue.
settings_dev_gitlab_desc: Link a GitLab project (gitlab.com or self-hosted) so merge requests and commits update issues, with pipeline and approval status on each issue.
settings_dev_owners_only: Only project owners and admins can change these connections.
settings_dev_sentry_description: Turn Sentry issue alerts into triage issues — one per Sentry issue, with the culprit, event count and a link — and note on the issue when Sentry marks it resolved. To link an existing Sentry issue, paste its URL as a link on the issue.
settings_dev_sentry_disconnect_desc: Alerts stop creating issues here. Issues already created and their Sentry links are kept.
settings_dev_sentry_secret_hint: Verifies that webhooks really come from your Sentry integration.
settings_dev_sentry_step1: In Sentry, open Settings → Custom Integrations → Create New Integration and choose Internal Integration.
settings_dev_sentry_step3: Turn on Alert Rule Action, give it Issue & Event: Read, and under Webhooks subscribe to issue (for resolves). Save.
settings_dev_sentry_step4: Paste the integration's Client Secret below (and a token for event counts).
settings_dev_sentry_step5: In an issue alert rule, add the action Send a notification via <your integration>.
settings_dev_sentry_token_hint: The integration's token. Lets new issues include the Sentry short ID and event / user counts.
settings_dev_username_hint: Only for API tokens (your Atlassian email) or app passwords (your Bitbucket username).
settings_dev_vcs_automation_desc: {description} Issues move with the {link} states from the GitHub settings.
settings_dev_vcs_disconnect_desc_bitbuck: The webhook is removed from Bitbucket and pull requests stop updating issues. Existing links on issues are kept.
settings_dev_vcs_disconnect_desc_gitlab: The webhook is removed from GitLab and merge requests stop updating issues. Existing links on issues are kept.
settings_dev_vcs_token_hint_bitbucket: A repository or workspace access token with webhook and pullrequest read access — or an API token / app password together with your username below. It's encrypted and used for the webhook and build statuses.
settings_dev_vcs_token_hint_gitlab: A personal, group or project access token with the api scope, from someone with the Maintainer role (needed to add the webhook). It's encrypted and only used to manage the webhook.
settings_dev_webhook_not_registered_bitb: Webhook not registered — pull requests won't update issues.
settings_dev_webhook_not_registered_gitl: Webhook not registered — merge requests won't update issues.
settings_dev_webhook_unreachable: Webhooks can't reach {url}. Connections still save, but automation needs a public URL — set PUBLIC_APP_URL (or GITHUB_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL for a tunnel) and register the webhooks again.
settings_github_account_desc: Branches and webhooks are created with your own GitHub authorization ({scopes}). Your token never leaves the server.
settings_github_auth_expired: Your GitHub authorization expired or was revoked.
settings_github_automation_desc: Move issues when a linked pull request changes. Issues are linked by their ID in the branch name or PR title, or with magic words like “Fixes {example}” in the description. Issues only move forward — never out of a completed or canceled state.
settings_github_connect_account_first: Connect your GitHub account with repository access first
settings_github_connect_account_hint: Connect your GitHub account with repository access above to pick a repository.
settings_github_connect_failed: Could not start the GitHub connection.
settings_github_disconnect_desc: The webhook is removed from GitHub and pull requests stop updating issues. Existing links and branch names on issues are kept.
settings_github_grant_hint: Grant repository access to connect repositories and create branches.
settings_github_not_set_up: GitHub isn't set up on this server. An admin needs to create a GitHub OAuth app and set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, then restart (see docs/SELF_HOSTING.md).
settings_github_owners_only: Only project owners and admins can change the GitHub connection.
settings_github_pr_merge: When a pull request is merged
settings_github_pr_merge_hint: Also applies to commits on the default branch that say “Fixes {example}”. “Ref {example}” or “Part of {example}” only link.
settings_github_pr_open: When a pull request is opened
settings_github_pr_open_hint: Drafts wait until they're marked ready for review.
settings_github_repo_desc: Issues link to pull requests in this repository, and branches are created here.
settings_github_unreachable: GitHub couldn't be reached. Reload to try again.
settings_github_webhook_missing: The webhook was removed on GitHub. Register it again to keep pull requests in sync.
settings_github_webhook_not_registered: Webhook not registered — pull requests won't update issues.
settings_github_webhook_outdated: The webhook doesn't send review and CI events yet, so pull requests can't show approval and check status.
settings_github_webhook_unreachable: GitHub can't deliver webhooks to {url}. Branches still work, but pull request automation needs a public URL — set PUBLIC_APP_URL (or GITHUB_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL for a tunnel) and register the webhook again.
settings_int_copy_failed_toast: Copy failed — the text is selected, copy it manually
settings_int_copy_key_desc: This is the only time the key is shown. Store it somewhere safe — anyone with it can act as you in every project you belong to.
settings_int_create_key_desc: The key acts as you, with your project roles.
settings_int_intake_accept_default: Anyone with the link can submit a request without an account. Requests arrive as issues in your default state (turn on triage in Cycles & triage to review them first).
settings_int_intake_accept_triage: Anyone with the link can submit a request without an account. Requests arrive as issues in Triage.
settings_int_intake_customers: When the submitter’s email domain matches one of your {link}, the request is linked to that customer automatically.
settings_int_intake_details_hint: Steps to reproduce, links, what you expected — anything that helps.
settings_int_intake_thanks_hint: The team will review it and follow up by email if they need more details.
settings_int_no_api_keys_hint: Create a key to script issues from CI, bots or your own tools.
settings_int_revoke_desc: Requests using this key will fail immediately. This can’t be undone.
settings_int_rotate_desc: The current link and any embedded forms stop working immediately.
settings_int_slack_post_desc: Post issue activity to a channel through a Slack {link}.
settings_oauth_authorized_desc: Apps that can access your account. Revoking signs them out everywhere.
settings_oauth_cc_run: Run this, then {command} in Claude Code to sign in:
settings_oauth_chatgpt_1: Open chatgpt.com/plugins → + → Add custom MCP server.
settings_oauth_chatgpt_2: Paste the URL above and choose OAuth.
settings_oauth_chatgpt_3: Sign in here and allow access.
settings_oauth_claude_2: Paste the URL above and add it.
settings_oauth_claude_3: Click Connect, sign in here and allow access.
settings_oauth_confidential_desc: A server that can keep a client secret.
settings_oauth_connect_ai_desc: Let Claude, ChatGPT or another MCP client read your issues and, with your permission, create issues, update them and comment as you. Workspace admins can block this per workspace.
settings_oauth_consent_expired: This authorization request expired or is invalid. Start again from the app.
settings_oauth_delete_desc: Everyone who connected this app loses access and its tokens are revoked. This can’t be undone.
settings_oauth_disabled_hint: This app can't be used. Delete it and register it again if you need it.
settings_oauth_dynamic_warning: This app registered itself. Its name isn’t verified: only continue if you started this from {where}.
settings_oauth_invalid_request_desc: The link expired or the app no longer exists. Go back to the app and try connecting again.
settings_oauth_no_browser: For agents without a browser, use a personal API key (Settings → API keys): {header}. Revoke an assistant’s access anytime under Authorized apps below.
settings_oauth_none_authorized_hint: Apps you allow through “Sign in with Ticket System” show up here.
settings_oauth_none_hint: Register an app to get a client ID for the OAuth authorization flow.
settings_oauth_public_desc: A single-page, desktop or mobile app — no secret, PKCE only.
settings_oauth_public_no_secret: Public apps have no secret: use PKCE (S256) on every authorization.
settings_oauth_redirect_hint: One per line, up to {max}. https, or http for localhost.
settings_oauth_register_desc: People see the name and logo when they authorize your app.
settings_oauth_revoke_anytime: Revoke access anytime in Settings → OAuth apps.
settings_oauth_revoke_desc: Its access and refresh tokens stop working immediately. You can authorize it again later.
settings_oauth_rotate_desc: The current secret stops working immediately; update your app with the new one.
settings_oauth_secret_once: Copy the secret now — it is shown only once and only a hash is stored.
settings_oauth_your_apps_desc: Apps you built that other people can connect to their account.
settings_sec_2fa_no_password: Two-factor authentication protects password sign-in. You sign in with GitHub, Google or single sign-on, so the two-factor settings of that account apply.
settings_sec_2fa_off_desc: Ask for a 6-digit code from an app like 1Password, Google Authenticator or Authy after your password.
settings_sec_2fa_on_desc: Password sign-ins ask for a 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or a backup code.
settings_sec_add_authenticator_desc: In your app, add an account with a setup key (time-based), then enter the code it shows. {link} on this device.
settings_sec_ai_allowed_desc: Members can connect Claude, ChatGPT or other AI assistants (MCP) and let them read and update this workspace’s issues on their behalf.
settings_sec_ai_blocked_desc: AI assistants connected by members can’t see or change anything in this workspace. Members’ projects outside it are not affected.
settings_sec_all_signed_out_toast: Signed out of all other sessions
settings_sec_code_mismatch: That code didn’t match. Check the time on your phone and try the next code.
settings_sec_codes_copy_failed: Copy failed — select the codes and copy them manually
settings_sec_disable_desc: Password sign-ins will no longer ask for a code. Your backup codes stop working.
settings_sec_dns_dev: Skipped in development. In production, prove the domain with this DNS record (keep it published — SSO stops trusting the domain if it is removed):
settings_sec_dns_prod: Add this DNS TXT record and keep it published — SSO stops trusting the domain if it is removed:
settings_sec_email_domain_hint: People with this email domain (and its subdomains) sign in through this provider.
settings_sec_enter_code: Enter the 6-digit code from your app.
settings_sec_give_idp: Give these to your identity provider
settings_sec_give_this_idp: Give this to your identity provider
settings_sec_keep_cert: Leave blank to keep the saved certificate.
settings_sec_keep_metadata: Leave blank to keep the saved metadata.
settings_sec_keep_secret: Leave blank to keep the current secret.
settings_sec_metadata_hint: Okta: Sign On → Metadata URL (open it and copy). Keycloak: realm → Endpoints → SAML 2.0 Identity Provider Metadata.
settings_sec_nameid_note: Name ID format: email address. Service provider metadata is served at the entity ID URL once saved.
settings_sec_new_codes_desc: Your old codes no longer work. This is the only time these are shown.
settings_sec_oidc_kc_1: Create a realm and a client (OpenID Connect, Client authentication on, Standard flow). Valid redirect URI = the redirect URI above. Issuer = `http://localhost:8080/realms/<realm>`. Give test users an email on your domain with “Email verified” on.
settings_sec_oidc_kc_2: Local IdP hosts are private addresses: add them to `BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` (e.g. `http://localhost:8080`) so discovery is allowed.
settings_sec_oidc_okta: Applications → Create App Integration → **OIDC – Web Application**. Sign-in redirect URI = the redirect URI above; grant type Authorization Code. Assign people, then copy the client ID and secret. Issuer = your Okta domain, e.g. `https://integrator-123.okta.com`.
settings_sec_regen_desc: Your current backup codes stop working immediately.
settings_sec_require_sso_desc: People with @{domain} emails can’t sign in or sign up with a password or GitHub — only through your identity provider.
settings_sec_saml_kc_1: Clients → Create client → **SAML**; Client ID = SP entity ID. Valid redirect URI and “Assertion Consumer Service POST Binding URL” = ACS URL. Name ID format `email`; turn on “Sign assertions”.
settings_sec_saml_kc_2: Client scopes → dedicated scope → add mappers: User Property `email` → `email`, and a Hardcoded attribute `email_verified` = `true`. Metadata: `http://localhost:8080/realms/<realm>/protocol/saml/descriptor`.
settings_sec_saml_okta_1: Applications → Create App Integration → **SAML 2.0**. Single sign-on URL = ACS URL, Audience URI = SP entity ID, Name ID format `EmailAddress`, Application username `Email`.
settings_sec_saml_okta_2: Attribute statements: `email` → `user.email`, `givenName` → `user.firstName`, `surname` → `user.lastName`, and `email_verified` → `"true"` (lets SSO sign in people who already have an account here).
settings_sec_saml_okta_3: Assign people, then paste the app’s metadata XML above.
settings_sec_save_codes_desc: If you lose your phone, each code signs you in once. This is the only time they’re shown — store them in your password manager.
settings_sec_scim_copy_desc: This is the only time it’s shown. Paste it into your identity provider as the bearer token — anyone with it can add and remove workspace members.
settings_sec_scim_desc: Your identity provider adds people to the workspace when they’re assigned and removes them from the workspace and its teams when they’re deactivated.
settings_sec_scim_domain: New users must use an email on the workspace’s SSO domain (when SSO is set up). An existing account is adopted only if it’s already a member or on that domain.
settings_sec_scim_keycloak_1: Keycloak has no built-in SCIM client — use a SCIM extension, or try the API directly:
settings_sec_scim_okta_1: In your app integration: General → Provisioning: **SCIM**. Provisioning tab → SCIM connector base URL `{baseUrl}`, unique identifier field `userName`, actions: Push New Users, Push Profile Updates; authentication **HTTP Header** with the token. Then To App → enable Create / Update / Deactivate Users.
settings_sec_scim_okta_2: Assigning a person provisions them as a workspace member; unassigning or deactivating removes them from the workspace and its teams and signs them out.
settings_sec_scim_revoke_desc: Provisioning stops immediately. Existing members stay in the workspace.
settings_sec_scim_rotate_desc: The current token stops working immediately; update your identity provider with the new one.
settings_sec_sessions_note: Signed-out devices lose access within 5 minutes.
settings_sec_sso_link_note: Existing accounts link on first SSO sign-in; a password set up without a verified email is removed then.

match.countPlural=one: {count} member has signed in with SSO.
match.countPlural=other: {count} members have signed in with SSO.

settings_sec_sso_no_members: No members have signed in with SSO yet.
settings_sec_sso_off_desc: Connect Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace, Keycloak or any SAML 2.0 / OIDC identity provider below.
settings_sec_sso_remove_desc: Members can no longer sign in through your identity provider, and SSO stops being required. People who only ever used SSO can’t sign in until it’s set up again.
settings_sec_two_factor_rate_limited: Too many attempts — wait a few seconds and try again.

match.countPlural=one: {count} member on @{domain} hasn’t verified their email.
match.countPlural=other: {count} members on @{domain} haven’t verified their email.

settings_sec_unverified_note: Their first SSO sign-in secures the account: it removes their password, two-factor, API keys, connected apps, linked Google/GitHub sign-ins, Slack link, push subscriptions and pending invitations (they get an email listing what went). Ask them to sign in with their password and verify their email first.
settings_wh_dialog_desc: Deliveries time out after 5 seconds. Failures are retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h and 12 h.
settings_wh_intro: Send a signed JSON POST to your endpoint whenever issues change. Verify X-Webhook-Signature with the secret.
settings_wh_no_deliveries_hint: Deliveries appear here as issue events are sent. Try “Send test”.
settings_wh_none_hint: Connect your own services to issue events.
settings_wh_none_selected: None selected — every event is sent.
settings_wh_signing_desc: Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with this secret and compare it to the X-Webhook-Signature header (sha256=…).
